data.caption: Wasn't NMN banned? Here is what actually happened.
data.copy:
You saw the headlines. "NMN banned." "FDA cracks down." "Is your supplement illegal?"

If you've been confused about the legal status of NMN over the last few years, you are not alone. The story was everywhere.

But the headlines skipped the most important part.

The FDA's initial 2022 decision was based on a technicality regarding a pharmaceutical drug filing, not a single safety finding. It caused real disruption in the market. Amazon pulled products. Processors backed away.

What most people missed is what happened next.

Industry groups fought back in federal court, proving NMN was sold as a supplement before the drug filing. In September 2025, the FDA officially reversed its position.

NMN was never found unsafe. There was a real regulatory fight, and NMN won it. As of 2026, it is a fully lawful dietary supplement again.

We put together a complete, 4 minute breakdown of the FDA timeline, the NMN vs NR debate, and the absorption problem nobody in the industry wants to talk about.

No pitch until you have the facts. Read the full timeline.

I helped my wife out of the bathtub for the first time eight months ago.

She didn't ask me to. I heard her trying to get out and I heard the way she grabbed the towel bar and I just walked in and gave her my arm and neither of us said a word about it.

First the bathtub. Then the stairs. I started carrying the laundry basket because I could see it in her face when she lifted it even though she'd never say anything. I moved dishes down from the top shelf. She'd stopped reaching for them and was using paper plates rather than ask for help.

She stopped gardening. Stopped walking after dinner. Stopped getting on the floor with the grandkids.

I did the grocery shopping alone because the parking lot had a curb she didn't trust.

data.caption: He Threw Up Wood Pulp That Night
data.copy:
COFFEE WOOD IS A SCAM!!

At least that's what I thought after buying it twice and pulling wood shards out of my rug both times.

Turns out coffee wood isn't a scam.

But the "coffee wood" I bought on Amazon? Mystery wood from a third-party seller, dried fast and hot in a kiln until it cracked like glass. My dog had chunks off it in twenty minutes.

And the one I ordered from another website to replace it? A real brand with thousands of reviews. He snapped a piece off the end within days. I heard it happen from the next room.

Two sticks. Two scares. Almost seventy dollars. And a dog who still had nothing safe to chew.

My name is Susan Hale. I live in Columbus, Ohio with my husband.

We have a Lab mix named Duke. Sixty pounds of pure love with the strongest jaws I've ever seen on a dog. He's my whole world.

Duke needs to chew. Not wants. Needs. When he doesn't get to, he finds his own way. First it was a shoe. Then a chair leg. Then a whole section of baseboard while I was at work.

So I kept him stocked with chews. Mostly a hard nylon bone, because the package said it was for tough chewers.

Then at a routine checkup, the vet found it. A slab fracture on a back tooth. From the nylon bone.

Extraction under anesthesia. The bill was over $1,500.

Later I learned the tooth wasn't even the whole problem. As a dog gnaws a nylon bone, he shaves off tiny plastic flecks and swallows them. And it doesn't all pass through. In 2024, researchers at the University of New Mexico looked at tissue from 47 dogs and found microplastics in every single sample, the most common kind being the same plastic they make grocery bags out of. I'd been handing my dog a chew that cracked his tooth and left plastic behind in his body. That was the last nylon bone Duke ever had.

After that I tried everything else. Bully sticks. Duke loved them, but they were gone in thirty minutes, they cost a fortune, and the smell settled into my couch. Then I found out a bully stick is literally a dried bull…

data.copy:
I took this picture of my foot last Sunday night and I want you to really look at it.

That's what a 14-mile long run did to me. My feet used to look like that every single weekend for eight years.

Blisters between every toe. The ball of my foot the color of a raw steak. Skin peeling off in strips between my third and fourth toes on both feet. I sat on the bench by my front door, pulled my toes apart to inspect the damage, and I thought the same thing I'd thought a hundred Sundays before:

Maybe my body just isn't built for this anymore.

I'm a running coach. I've been one for eleven years. I run a small group out of our town — around 40 runners at any given time, ages 28 to 68, everyone from first-time 5K people to Boston qualifiers.

I want to tell you about a guy named Marcus, because Marcus is the reason I'm writing this.

Marcus came to me three years ago. He was 52. Recently divorced. Had gained about 30 pounds in the two years around the separation. Told me on our first phone call that he wanted to run a half marathon because his daughter was running one for a charity and he wanted to cross the finish line with her.

"I need to drop weight and I need to be able to run thirteen miles without completely wrecking myself," he said. "My daughter's race is in nine months. Can you help me."

I said yes. Because you don't say no to that.

For the first four months Marcus was crushing it. Lost 18 pounds. Got his easy pace from a 14-minute mile down to an 11. Mentally he was in the best place I'd ever seen him.

Then he showed up to a Tuesday workout limping.

"I can't do this one, coach. My feet."

He sat on the curb and took his shoes off and I swear to god I almost looked away.

His feet looked worse than mine in that picture. Way worse. Blisters the size of nickels between every toe. The skin on the balls of his feet was split open in two places. Between his fourth and fifth toes on the right foot, the skin was completely raw. You could see the tissue underneath…

By the end of that school year, he wasn't a kid who liked girls anymore.

He'd talk about the kids at his lunch table the way you'd talk about furniture. That was the first time I noticed.

Patient presents with chronic bloating. Doctor's notes: IBS. Recommend dietary modification.

Patient returns. Fatigue that sleep doesn't fix. Doctor's notes: Chronic fatigue. Blood panel normal. Recommend exercise.

Patient returns. Waking up at 3am every night. Heart pounding. Can't fall back asleep. Doctor's notes: Sleep disruption. Likely stress-related. Prescribe sleep aid.

Patient returns. Brain fog. Forgetting words. Can't follow conversations. Doctor's notes: Consider cognitive evaluation.

min.description: Minimum duplicate/active-seen ad count on the page.

minactiveads.description: Minimum active Meta ads on the advertiser Facebook page (total_active_ads_on_page).
minactiveads.notes: find_winning_products auto-applies minactiveads=50 for US when not set (see forced block).

minactiveadsgrowth.description: Minimum page active-ads percent growth over activeadsgrowthperiod.
minactiveadsgrowth.allowed_values: Human percent (25 = 25%); negatives allowed for decline.

activeadsgrowthperiod.description: Lookback window for active-ads growth filter.
activeadsgrowthperiod.allowed_values: 1w, 1m, 3m. Default 1m when min/max growth set. 1w=1 week, 1m=1 month, 3m=3 months.
activeadsgrowthperiod.notes: 14d/2m exist on the dashboard but are omitted from MCP — sparse wlads baselines return empty result sets.

minpagelikes.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. Ads missing the field excluded when min set.

minadspend.description: Minimum EU ad spend total in adspendtimeframe window.
minadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier; can return upgrade JSON.

maxadspend.description: Maximum EU ad spend in window.
maxadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. 999999 treated as no upper cap server-side.

adspendtimeframe.description: Rolling window ad spend is summed over (NOT a calendar month filter).

minreach.description: Minimum EU reach/views total in reachtimeframe window.
minreach.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

reachtimeframe.description: Rolling window reach is summed over.

mintraffic.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

minproductsonstore.description: Minimum published products on the Shopify store.

minprice.description: Minimum product price on landing page.

mincopylength.description: Minimum ad primary text character length.

minvideolength.description: Minimum video duration in seconds (use with mediafilter=videos).

mindays.description: Minimum days the ad has been running.
mindays.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

from.description: Ad launch date lower bound (Meta started field — when ad began running, NOT scrape date).
from.allowed_values: YYYY-MM-DD. Requires to on same range.

to.notes: To isolate ads running in a calendar month: ad_created_to=last day of month AND fromlastseen=first day of month.

product_from.description: Shopify product creation date lower bound.

pagefrom.description: Facebook page creation date lower bound.

activestatus.description: Legacy dashboard param (no longer applied to ES queries).
activestatus.allowed_values: Ignored — use adstatus or last_seen_from/to instead.

adstatus.description: Dashboard Status filter — recently seen vs stale ads.
adstatus.allowed_values: active (lastSeen or updated_at within last 4 days), inactive (neither field within last 4 days), All/empty (no status filter).
adstatus.notes: find_winning_products forces active. Same as dashboard Status = Active.

sorting.allowed_values: relevance, datefound, mostrecent, lastseen, adspend, longestrunning, reach, adsetamount, consistency, monthlyvisits, monthlytraffic, monthlyrevenue, pageactiveads, toprank, mostsaved. Aliases: rank/top_ad/best_ranked→toprank (asc = best rank first, desc = worst rank first). ad_started→mostrecent. monthly_visits→monthlyvisits. monthly_traffic→monthlytraffic.

page.description: Pagination page index (informational). Deep pagination requires scroll from the previous response — incrementing page alone does not advance the result set.
page.allowed_values: MCP uses 1-based page (1=first page); echoed value is 0-based internal page sent to API.

scroll.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Empty/omit on the first request; pass the response scroll value on the next request with the same filters to fetch more ads. Required to download beyond the first page (especially sort_by=lastseen).
scroll.allowed_values: Opaque string from previous response; empty string or omit for first page. Stop when scroll is null/absent or data is shorter than a full page.

allowed_apps: BOGOS.io Free Gift Buy X Get Y
KB Back In Stock Restock Alert
Sticky Add To Cart Booster Pro
POWR Email Popup Sales Pop Ups
EG Auto Add to Cart Free Gift
SA Request a Quote, Hide Price
Zoorix Sticky Add To Cart Bar
Tada Pop up Spin Wheel Popups
Coupon X: Discount Code Pop Up
SC Back in Stock Restock Alert

mcp_pagination.hint: Pass scroll_next as scroll on the next call with the same filters to continue. Do not rely on page alone.
